The Fortunes module's design note says it bundles zero fortune content and is silent until a pack is added, but the module embeds the 391 KB base corpus and loads it first in every standard pool; its 'Relocation plan' is also long done

The probe folds three sub-reports from fixed %TEMP% file names that nothing deletes first, so a sub-test that could not write its report folds the PREVIOUS run's report under this run's verdict, and two runs sharing a TEMP read each other's
The importer self-test's invalid-UTF-8 fixture is five characters long, so it is refused for having no valid row whatever the decoder does; the sub-case cannot notice a lenient decode

A plain (untagged) pack drops every entry outside 8..280 characters one by one with a bare continue: nothing counts the dropped rows, the importer and the download say the pack was added, and the pane's skip note (which counts FILES) stays silent
fix_direction: Count rows a plain pack drops for length and surface it (import status and the skip log line), e.g. 'Imported 1 pack (12 entries over 280 characters left out).'

title: The vector cache is pruned to the active pool on every warm and save, so narrowing the selection and widening it again re-embeds the dropped lines from scratch, while the class comment promises the pool is embedded once ever and survives pack changes
fix_direction: Correct the header to say the file is pruned to the active pool, and say in the pane that changing the selection can re-embed. Alternatively keep a bounded LRU of recently inactive vectors so a toggle back is a cache hit.

title: The csproj comment on the embedded corpus describes the pre-shrink corpus: it claims 26 sources and ~10k lines, seven of them in no pack file, while the embedded fortunes.txt has had 2 sources and 3,225 rows since d71de2e (2026-09-09)

The two speech paths share history in one direction only: a line the smart picker just spoke is never removed from (or marked in) the shuffle bag, so the next random draw can repeat it back to back, and the bag's 'every line once before any repeats' guarantee does not hold while smart picks are on
'Installed' means 'loaded', not 'on disk': a pack file the loader refused is listed again under Available online, and Download selected then overwrites that file in place with no check or prompt
The comment says an offline machine backs off for the whole week, but a failed fetch is never stamped, so an offline machine retries on every launch

One stop of the user's CHOSEN device moves all audio to the default for the rest of the session: _chosenDeviceFailed is cleared only by SetDevice or the _unavailable retry, and that retry never runs while the default keeps working

The comment says NAudio's Stop aborts the playback thread when it cannot take its lock; the pinned NAudio 3.0.0-preview.6 only nulls notifyThread, so a torn-down output whose lock stayed busy keeps its playback thread running
fix_direction: Rewrite the comment to say what preview.6 actually does: a lost TryEnter leaves the thread running. Optionally, after Dispose, check o.PlaybackState and log or retry Stop when it is still Playing.

title: The encoded-size pre-check counts whitespace that Convert.FromBase64String ignores, with a fixed 4096-character slack, so a line-wrapped base64 payload within about 2.5% of its decoded cap is refused as 'exceeds its encoded size limit' although it decodes inside the limit

The second allowed instance shares the data root, so its launch rotation moves the first instance's live log to .1 mid-run, the keep trim then deletes the previous run's log, and both instances append untagged lines to one file

FactoryReset claims it refuses a path that is 'simply not where this app keeps things', but IsSafeToWipe checks only depth and an exact list of special folders, so an overridden data root is emptied whatever else it holds
An alpha tick companion re-pushes its frame through GetHbitmap + UpdateLayeredWindow on every 40 ms tick even when the frame, position and opacity are unchanged

A right-side window grip is pinned with the FORM's current Width, which the colour-key clip branch shrinks, so a colour-key pet gripping the right side of a window near the screen's right edge is pushed further right by its own clip every tick and collapses to a 1-pixel, invisible form (latent on the shipped corpus)

RiseDetect enumerates every top-level window (EnumWindows plus GetWindowText and GetTitleBarInfo per visible window) on every upward tick of every classic pet, including the 22 hand-authored pets that declare no window-bottom edge at all, whose result is then always discarded
The validator accepts a sequence action of 'flip' in any letter case, but the engine flips only on the exact lowercase string, so action 'Flip' loads and silently never turns the pet

RiseDetect copies FallDetect's 'Sheep' title exemption, which exists to let a falling pet land on another pet, so a jumping converted pet can catch the underside of ANOTHER companion's mostly transparent cell and hang from it in mid-air, carried along as that companion moves
fix_direction: In RiseDetect, skip windows titled "Sheep" (companion forms) instead of exempting them, or test against the other pet's visible insets rather than its cell rect.

title: The classic window grips measure windows with GetWindowRect, which on Windows 10/11 includes the invisible resize border on the left, right and bottom, so a pet hangs that far below a window's visible underside and clings that far outside its visible sides; the tick runtime and DesktopWindows use DWM extended frame bounds for exactly this reason

FollowWindow carries a pet by shifting the FORM's Left/Top and the caller then reads the logical position back from them, so a colour-key pet whose form is clipped at the work-area edge jumps by the clip amount (leftCut or topCut) the first time its window moves

CheckTopWindow decides whether a window covers the surface a pet stands on by testing the fixed span [PositionX, PositionX + 40], eSheep's 40 px width, so for any wider or padded pet it tests the wrong strip: an occluder over the character is missed and one over the transparent padding drops the pet
The narrowed catches in HotkeyRegistrarSmoke are unreachable, and their comment's claim that narrowing makes a NullReferenceException inside RegisterHotkey visible is false

Rolling back a failed Init removes a CredentialChanged handler from the event but not from _credentialHandlerOwners, so the map keeps the failed module's delegate (and its collectible AssemblyLoadContext) alive
SafeId maps distinct module ids to one data folder, so two modules can share storage and uninstalling one deletes the other's data

IModuleSettings.Save truncates settings.json in place, and Load silently returns an empty dictionary for a damaged file, so a failed or interrupted save resets every setting of the module with no log line
MemSettings' doc says 'A fresh store per call', but RecordingHost.GetSettings keeps one store per module id across calls, and the bulk-selection checks depend on that
fix_direction: Change the summary to say the store is created once per module id by RecordingHost.GetSettings and kept across calls, seeded with smartFortunes=false.

title: A read racing a commit re-caches the plaintext of the token the commit just replaced or removed, undoing ForgetUnsealed (A-host-05) until some later read happens

The 'Shutdown unsubscribed every host event' check says 'Six of six' and claims to cover every loadable module, but the convention host does not implement IHostCredentials, so the seventh host event, CredentialChanged, is never offered and a leaked handler on it passes

System.Version comparison counts components, so a MinHostVersion of '1.11.0.0' refuses host '1.11.0' ('needs host 1.11.0.0 or newer (this host is 1.11.0)') and a single-component '2' is treated as a typo and ignored
InitRollback proves a failed Init loses its tray items, pane, subscriptions and responders, but not a tray question it asked; the ledgered CancelModule in CompanionHost.AskAsync has no check anywhere
'no log line carries a value' covers only the first credential store; the stores that exercise NotAToken, Unreadable, DPAPI failure, lock-timeout and the import race are built with a null logger

An uninstall deletes the data folder and forgets the sign-in grant of the FOLDER name, so a module whose folder name differs from its Info.Id keeps its settings, keys and Claude Code grant after uninstall
A resource-churn soak whose marker write throws never exits: Finish sets 'finished' before WriteMarker, so the catch's Finish(false, ex) returns at once and no exit timer is armed
CatalogText.Echo replaces every UTF-16 surrogate, not only lone ones as its summary says, so an emoji in an echoed catalog name renders as '??'
fix_direction: Either let well-formed pairs through (check char.IsSurrogatePair(value, i) and copy both chars, with the max check counting the pair) or change the summary to say that every surrogate is replaced.

title: --online-selftest passes a live catalog that offers nothing: with zero pets and zero packs (or every entry refused by the parser) no download is verified and ok stays true; modules and Rejected are never looked at

SafeScript reads a leading-zero integer literal as decimal (010 is 10) where Nashorn's non-strict JS reads it as legacy octal (010 is 8), though the same lexer refuses octal string escapes by name, so the one octal form gets a silently different value instead of a refusal
The tray's 'Remove a companion' row counts only chosen pets, but its click removes the most recent pet of that id, which is often a session-only born companion
KillSheeps says 'a modal cannot outlive the exit request', but CloseOpenWindow closes only the Options window; the tray's modal About window stays up through the exit

The 'answer's continuation runs asynchronously, never inside the host's click handler' check tests the self-test's own TaskCompletionSource, not the host's; the host's option is guarded only by a source-text invariant

The log privacy check reads the log of only two of the ~20 rigs, so the arbiter's refused (unknown-module, duplicate-key, too-many-pending, rate-limited), withdrawn, cancelled and expired log lines are never inspected

The F375/RA-329 checks cover a ReloadPaneAfter action finishing after a pane switch and after a same-pane return, but not after the window CLOSED, so the '_closed ||' half of the reload guard (OptionsWindow.cs:370) can be deleted with every check passing

The window's refresh-after-Apply rule (rebuild a pane with an Info OR Header row, leave every other pane alone) is exercised only on panes holding an Info row, so deleting the Header clause or making RefreshAfterApply always true passes --wpf-options-selftest

ModulesPaneProbe sets CountsAsLoaded = true for every case, so the Modules pane's 'pane went away during the download' branches (IsUp false) and its Unloaded cancel run under no check: deleting any of them passes --wpf-options-selftest

The window's containment of a pane whose build throws ('This pane failed to load: ...', OptionsWindow.cs:387-388) runs under no check: the self-test already has a throwing pane (ThrowingOptionsSchema) but calls SchemaShellPane.BuildContent directly and never puts it in a window
fix_direction: Build an OptionsWindow over SchemaShellPane(failingPane) and assert that CurrentContent is a TextBlock whose text starts with 'This pane failed to load'. Add a guard mutation that removes the catch at OptionsWindow.cs:388.

title: 'the gallery of classic companions shows no switch' builds the Pets pane over whatever library the run's data root holds, so it fails falsely wherever a tick-clock companion is installed and passes only because the gate's library is classic
The 64 MiB generated-bytes check in ValidateSpriteBudget can never fire: it runs after the 16 Mi pixel check, and 16 Mi pixels x 4 bytes is exactly 64 MiB
The future-schema warning tells the user to 'move the file aside to start fresh', but LoadCore then reads settings.json.bak, which the newer build also wrote, so the session stays read-only

A module that LOADS fine from a folder whose name differs from its Info.Id reads 'installed, restart to activate' forever, with no version, no update offer and no sign-in row: the pane looks rows up by folder name in LoadedModules (by Info.Id), and ModuleHost records no failure for a successful load
fix_direction: Have ModuleHost record the folder each loaded module came from and key the pane's live lookup by it. Also flag or refuse a module whose Info.Id differs from its folder, or duplicates a loaded id.

title: A module whose uninstall is pending (restart declined) renders as an ordinary installed row with its live version and an enabled Update button and nothing saying it will be removed, so a later row Update silently cancels the uninstall

The Reinstall button on a module that failed to load never asks the loader's MinHostVersion question, so it offers, downloads and swaps in a catalog build this host will refuse, contradicting the class doc 'No row offers a build whose MinHostVersion this host cannot satisfy'
Preferences shows volume rounded to tenths and Apply always writes the rounded value back, so a stored volume off the 0.1 grid is silently changed by any unrelated Apply
fix_direction: In Save, skip SetVolume when the posted tenth equals the rounded stored value (or compare against what Load showed), so an untouched field keeps the stored volume.

title: Assert-ScopedShutdownPath refuses a reparse point anywhere from the DRIVE ROOT down, including the checkout root and its ancestors, so since 2026-10-23 build-installer.ps1 again fails on a checkout reached through a junction, the case F218 (2026-09-30) fixed in the packaging helper and pinned in Test-StagingPathSafety.ps1

The 7-only rationale of the portable-ZIP script (copied from the module-zip script) says these archives are committed, served off master and hashed in catalog.json; the portable ZIP is none of those, and build.ps1 repeats the claim in its comment and in the error it throws at a 5.1 user

The -Commit path runs a bare `git commit`, so it commits the WHOLE index (anything else already staged lands in 'chore(modules): publish <id> <ver>'), and on a re-run after step 5 failed it throws 'git commit failed (exit 1)' because there is nothing new to commit

The cleanup comment credits 'the reparse chain check' with guarding Remove-Item -Recurse -Force, but the guard it calls (Assert-DesktopAICompanionPathChainSafe) only tests string containment and has never walked reparse points, and Remove-DesktopAICompanionSafeDirectory does not test the target itself either

The dead-child witness can fail CI on a timing race: if cmd.exe /c exit 1 has already exited when Get-CatalogAsset flushes its request, the Flush throws a broken-pipe IOException, which is reported as 'could not talk to the child' instead of 'exited or closed its output', and the witness throws

Check 2 says the catalog must match 'the newest RELEASED tag', but it reads every local v* tag with no release behind it, so a tag whose release.yml run failed (or is still running) turns master's CI red and pushes the maintainer to publish an app.version that has nothing to download

The template check claims to leave the machine as it found it, but it uninstalls the template unconditionally, so an author who installed it per docs/module-authoring.md loses their install after running the check that same page tells them to run
fix_direction: Before installing, probe 'dotnet new uninstall' (list mode) or 'dotnet new list desktop-ai-companion-module' for the template's source, and uninstall in the finally only if this run made the install. Otherwise correct the header claim.

title: The template teaches that after a failed Save() 'the pane reads back what the disk still holds, not the edit that never landed', and asserts it, but that holds only under FakeModuleSettings: the shipped host's settings object keeps Set() values in memory, and the template's one held handle then reads the unsaved edit back

The comparer's build-witness check only shape-checks oracle provenance: sourceZipSha256, patchSha256, jdk and deps are never compared with anything, and artifactSha256/exeSha256 only when a flag nobody passes is given
fix_direction: Have the comparer check the oracle witness against the pinned SOURCE_SHA256 and the repository patch hash (shared with oracle.py), or reword the docstring to say the witness is shape-checked and bound only through --oracle-artifact/--host-exe.

title: State fields compare with Python equality, under which JSON true equals 1, while events compare by json.dumps, under which 1 and 1.0 differ: the two halves of one comparer disagree on what 'exact' means
The origin tolerance zips two unvalidated lists, so an empty or one-element origin passes as within-tolerance
The tolerance verdict names only the last tolerance used, so a run that relied on both reports one
The comparer's --self-test, its only proof that it can fail, is run by no gate, CI step or oracle self-test
fix_direction: Run 'python tools/ShimejiParity/comparer/compare.py --self-test' from tests/Invoke-OfflineScriptChecks.ps1 (which CI runs) and fail on a non-zero exit or a missing 'SELF-TEST PASS' line.

title: A free-running time-share pass exits 0, which the docstring reserves for parity

The scenario generator never clears its output folder, so a re-run into a used folder keeps files an earlier generator version wrote and the packs' content (and packSha256) then depend on the folder's history
The rename of older by-date captures leaves a 2.8.0 follow-up file ('<old base> - follow-up.md') behind under the old name, splitting the capture the rename promises to move whole

The one-call limit's comment says whisper's own limit on one recording is six hours (Transcriber.MaximumWhisperTimeout), but that constant caps whisper's RUN time, not a recording's length, and recordings can run 8 h and be extended without bound
fix_direction: Rewrite the comment: recordings can run 8 h or more with extensions, and a stop-path transcript over 360 KB takes the local map-reduce or reports that none is set. Drop the reference to MaximumWhisperTimeout.

title: One saved cloud API key is sent as a Bearer token to whichever provider or custom base URL is on screen, so a key saved for one provider reaches another host on a Refresh, Validate or summary

With 'The follow-up reads' set to summary and transcript, a follow-up on a summary made by 'Summarize a transcript...' from any .txt not named '*.transcript.txt' always fails, and says the transcript 'could not be read' when it does not exist

The Permissions comment says Network is for 'two user-initiated local/upstream calls' (the Whisper download and a LOOPBACK Ollama), but since 2.2.0 the module itself sends every transcript to a cloud provider over HTTPS, and the Ollama address is any URL
A snapshot that fails before its capture starts (no usable storage folder, a folder that cannot be created) is only logged: the user who pressed the hotkey hears and sees nothing

'Transcribe a WAV file...' opens its own WinForms OpenFileDialog instead of the host's PickFilesToOpen seam, so no self-test can press it: its busy span, its output path and its stub-overwrite are unverified

The WITNESS that this machine's Network Protection value 'is one the interpreter accepts' cannot fail: NetworkProtectionState returns only what InterpretNetworkProtectionValue already accepted (0..2) or null

The save-reporting check asserts that a failed settings write leaves the OLD Whisper paths, which only the fake does; under the shipped host the module keeps the new paths, which is what its own '...applies to this session only' message says

The 'no log line carries the prompts, the transcript, the summary or the follow-up's answer' check only sees lines logged after the second ClearLoggedLines, so the recording-stop summary on the user's own prompt file, its automatic follow-up and the failed-follow-up branch are never checked for leaks
fix_direction: Snapshot host.LoggedLines before the :408 clear and assert the same sentinel-free condition over it, or move the :408 clear's own assertions to a filtered view instead of clearing.

title: Every options-pane Load walks the whole storage root and each day folder (PlanRenames) synchronously to fill the 'Older recordings' line, so a storage folder on a slow or offline share stalls the pane each time it opens or reloads
A Join & record request that arrives while a recording runs is deferred, not dropped: it is not marked seen, so stopping that recording within a minute starts another one nobody asked for then
Join & record trusts an unauthenticated shared-context key: any loaded module can publish meeting.record-request and Remembrance starts a microphone and system-audio recording within 5 s
fix_direction: Correct the comment to say requests are trusted by convention, or have Remembrance confirm a context-triggered start with a tray question before recording.

title: whisper-cli's own output file is deleted before the transcript is written, and a transcript write that then fails is swallowed while the caller announces 'Transcript ready.'
TryVerify kills a whisper-cli that overran its five minutes and deletes its scratch folder at once, without waiting for the kill, so the folder (and check.wav) can be left in %TEMP% for good
Refresh staleness and the stall deadline are measured on the wall clock, so a clock set back stops every feed refreshing (and hides a hung one) for the size of the jump

The Reminder local-feed contract says `end` and `location` are 'Not used yet' and documents no other event fields; the reader uses both and also reads description, allDay, status and attendees, which the contract never mentions
'at HH:mm' and bare 'HH:mm' reminders that roll to tomorrow keep today's UTC offset, so across a DST change they fire an hour early or late
'Stay quiet while presenting' (on by default) hushes reminders under ANY fullscreen window, and a reminder whose window passes while hushed is dropped with no log line
fix_direction: Log the hush hold once per hold with its cause, as NoteHeld does for the no-companion hold, and relabel the setting to say it also covers fullscreen apps. Alternatively, limit the hush to QUNS_PRESENTATION_MODE/D3D and leave plain QUNS_BUSY to an opt-in.

title: With the default 'Skip all-day events' off, every all-day event gets a lead reminder at its midnight start: a chime and 'Offsite starts in 5 minutes.' at 23:55 the night before
fix_direction: Skip e.AllDay in the lead-reminder path (before DueNowMulti), matching CheckJoinPrompts, and keep all-day events in the agenda and the morning briefing.

title: The self-test's question host models the four-pending limit but not the host's six-asks-a-minute limit, so the module's per-minute guard can be deleted with every 'one the host would take' check still green
A tick that lands inside two lead windows at once (wake from sleep, launch, end of a hold) announces the same meeting twice in one tick, with identical text, two chimes and two reactions
CodingAgentCliException builds its message with no timeout, so a CLI timeout under AI Brain's user-set bound is described as 'did not answer within 120 s'
The three-argument Interpret overload has no caller, and any caller it gained would silently turn off every refused- and ignored-setting reading, since it passes null arguments

OutcomeWord and Brief(CliOutcome) have no case for TokenNotAllowed or TokenStoreUnavailable (added in 9001b9b, host 1.8.0), so both fall to 'failed' in the log, AI Brain's Status card and the CLI card's Status row
Only a Codex screenshot call that ANSWERED is checked for its call folder being deleted; no check covers the screenshot's deletion after a timeout or a cancel
fix_direction: Add two checks: a Codex screenshot call held past its Timeout, and one cancelled mid-call. Each asserts that the call's folder (the ImagePath parent the fake saw) no longer exists. Pair them with a mutation that wraps DeleteQuietly in if (exited).

title: The self-check 'this app's own recording never counts as a meeting app holding the microphone' asserts only that For(MeetingApp.None) is null, which MicUseSnapshot.For returns by construction, so it passes whatever Read() does with the app's own in-use key

The fullscreen stand-down check replaces FormCompanion.TickMonitorBlocked's whole body through TickBlockedForSelfTest, so the monitor mapping a tick window actually uses (FormCompanion.cs:385-411) runs under no self-test

The pack checks replace the app's member stager and binding wiring with test copies staged at a fixed 1.0, so the per-member size the app actually stages at, and AttachTickPacks' StageMember wrapper, are never exercised

The fault throttle keys on the full message, and several engine faults embed the offending runtime value, so one companion whose condition yields a changing non-boolean burns all 256 distinct slots in about ten seconds, after which every NEW fault of every tick companion is silently dropped until the app restarts

The tick clock never stops: once any tick companion has spawned, the 10 ms poll timer and a full 40 ms world step (EnumWindows walk, Screen.AllScreens, cursor read) run for the rest of the session even with zero tick companions left

Step opens a window for a companion that is already disposing: a birth that ends during its first tick (activated and ticked in the same StepOnce) still gets a new window, a pet-list slot and a registry reference, only to have them closed at the next step
'a looped chain builds' is written as FAIL but never folded into ok, so the host's --petstudio-selftest, which reads only RunChecks' bool, passes when the looped debug chain stops building

The replace path's 'Still installed from before, and no longer in this pack' branch cannot be reached, and an UPDATED pack is installed as a second copy under '-2' ids with no replace offered, because the pack id is a hash of every member's name and source bytes

When a REPLACE install stops part way, the message says the main member was not installed and that the installed members are listed on their own 'without the rest of the pack', though the earlier install's main member and the rest of the pack are still installed
Opening Companion Studio while its window is minimized only calls Activate, which does not restore a minimized WPF window, yet the pane reports 'Companion Studio is open.'

A later zip import that is cancelled or fails deletes the extraction tree under the pack report still on screen, so its 'Import with recovery' re-converts a folder that no longer exists and reports a false reason
fix_direction: When the zip path deletes the previous extraction tree, call ClosePackReport (or at least null _packRoot and collapse _recoverPackButton). Optionally also have RecoverPackClicked refuse when Directory.Exists(_packRoot) is false, with an accurate message.

title: A skin folder or zip holding exactly one character can never be imported for the Shimeji runtime: the pack button lives only in the multi-skin picker, which SelectSkin skips for one skin
Closing the window while a skin is being detected still starts the full conversion (sprite sheet build, one ffmpeg per clip, or dwebp per sprite for a bundle) for a window that is gone

The comment says every pack-mode status, the analysis verdict included, starts with the pack prefix, but Re-analyze in pack mode analyzes with an empty prefix and erases 'Converted with recovery: N dropped'
Picking a refused pack member while another member's analysis is in flight lets that analysis render over the cleared view: map, report, Preview button and status all describe the previous member
Install pack's outcome, including a partial install's list of what went in and under which ids, is written only to the status bar, where the member analysis still in flight overwrites it
NOTICE_NO_CHAIN looks for a chained notice in the recipient's queue, but a notice's own notice would be owed to the reserved notice sender, so removing the no-chain guard leaves the check green
The mDNS reply negatives assert SendCount as soon as the fake transport hands the packet over, before the discovery loop has decided whether to reply, so a mutant can pass by timing
The Network harness never deletes its scratch tree, on success as well as failure, so every run leaves about 20 broker state directories with DPAPI identity blobs under bin
The oversized-DNS check parses 1,401 zero bytes, which DnsSdCodec.Parse already rejects for having no response flag, so removing the 1,400-byte bound leaves it green

The control-listener-failure cleanup check counts an engine that has not yet written its PID as exited, and the relay fails within milliseconds of launching it, so the check passes whether or not the engine is killed
fix_direction: Make the witness able to fail: wait for launches.log with a timeout (or expose the relay's owned Process) and then assert that PID has exited, instead of treating an absent counter as exited.

title: The tombstone benchmark's history-count guard accepts the control's count on the candidate build too, so a candidate store that loaded none of the seeded journal tombstones passes and its loadMs and storeHeapBytes are reported as the cost of holding them

The directory benchmark says it 'checks completeness' and that every scenario asserts its measured operation did what it was timed doing, but it only records federated (and returned) and never compares them with expected, so a federated page cut short by the five-second budget is timed and reported as an ok sample

The firewall block checks exclude disabled, allow and outbound rules through CouldBlock, but the real COM backend excludes them with its own filter that no test runs, and the fake backend calls CouldBlock directly
LoopbackHostChecks and SendAdvisoryChecks start a real WorkerApplication in a fresh scratch folder and delete only its CNG key, so each gate run leaves two worker data directories under bin
McpActivityChecks never deletes its scratch data root, leaving a DPAPI-sealed broker identity file and a store behind on every run
Both keyset traversal loops have no iteration bound, so a regression that ignores the cursor hangs the harness instead of failing it
PeerForwardChecks creates a broker store under the test bin folder on every run and never deletes it; FirstContactChecks and CompactReceiptChecks do the same through ToolFixture
Worker harness scratch folders are never deleted: Program.cs's main scratch and MailboxChecks/ChannelBridgeChecks fixtures leave a broker store per run under bin/.../scratch

Four more Worker check files create per-run scratch trees under bin/.../scratch and never delete them: RuntimeLifecycleChecks.cs:14, PeerDiagnosticsChecks.cs:17, ReplyToolChecks.cs:11 and SendToolChecks.cs:78 (the last two delete only the CNG key in finally)

The two five-second-budget checks await the call under test with no bound, so the exact regression they exist to catch (the budget or the WaitAsync on a transport that ignores cancellation removed) hangs the run instead of failing a labelled check; same at PeerDiagnosticsChecks.cs:178

'late transport completions drain without publishing additional directory sessions' asserts only the fake's in-flight counter, which DrainAsync has already forced to zero (or thrown), and never looks at the directory results again, so late publication is not checked at all

CODEX_SLOW_ORDER_RECONNECT and CODEX_RECONNECT_KEPT assert exact renewal counts that hold only while wall-clock Task.Delay timers keep 100-200 ms margins, while the comments call the counts deterministic, so a loaded machine fails them on healthy code
ToolFixture creates a fresh scratch store per fixture but its DisposeAsync never removes it (32 fixtures across 8 check files)

"Child-position coordinate reproduction" re-does the child arithmetic inline (parentLocal + offset, then MonitorLocalToVirtual), so it only re-tests the converter pair TestMonitorLayouts already pins and cannot fail on the defect its label names: FormCompanion applying the monitor origin twice

No test adds two types that claim the same (pack, member) key, so TickWorld.IndexReference's first-registered-wins rule (TickPacks.cs:145-150) can be deleted with CoreTests and the mutation suite green
fix_direction: Add a CoreTests group that AddTypes two differently named types with one pack id and member key, then asserts ResolveReference still returns the first and ReferenceConflict fired once; add a matching mutate case for the early return.

title: The pack-index test cannot tell the documented case-insensitive folder order from a plain ordinal one, so CompanionPackIndex.cs:122 can be switched to Ordinal with every check green

The ScanMove arrival group claims 'only EXACT arrival (both axes, not turning)' runs the partner transitions, but every ScanMove fixture has seeker and target on one y and no turn variant, so the y half and the turning half of TickSocialFamily.cs:188 can be deleted with every check green

Only ScanMove has a 'target stopped offering' test; the same end-on-lost-target guard in ScanJump, scanning ComplexMove and scanning ComplexJump (TickSocialFamily.cs:231, :455, :568) can be deleted with CoreTests and the mutation suite green

TestTickSoundMuteNamed claims a named Mute stops the initiator's running clips 'at any volume', but its fixture has no running clip of the initiator at a non-zero volume, so a Mute that matched only 0 dB clips passes

The probe's 'call-for-call' replica of FullscreenScan predates the click-through rule (7c620d7, 2026-10-26): it never reads GWL_EXSTYLE and lets a click-through window decide a monitor, so its counts miss one Win32 call per window and its INCONCLUSIVE oracle can disagree with the app it grades
Every run creates a fresh artifacts/discovery-timeouts/<guid> tree (NuGet.Config, CLI home, NuGet package, HTTP and plugin caches, scratch) and nothing ever deletes it
The pattern-only check that exists to catch a mutation case guarding nothing (--check-patterns) is called by no gate, build or CI step, and mutate-diagnostics.py has no equivalent at all
fix_direction: Run `mutate-agentflow.py --check-patterns` (about 1 s, no build) from Invoke-OfflineScriptChecks.ps1 or run-gate.ps1, and give mutate-diagnostics.py the same flag and wiring.

title: Stranded mutant after a hard kill: the restore copy lives only in process memory and mutate-diagnostics is never run under the shard controller, so nothing detects or repairs a mutant left in src/
mutate-diagnostics prints no verdict until every case has run, so an interrupt, a build timeout or a capture error mid-run discards every verdict already measured, FIRED ones without any trace
On a DEGRADED baseline the 'DOC DRIFT' case is scored FIRED whatever its mutation does, because its expected text is the baseline's own failure line

The mutant ceiling comment says every later run of a flag gets four times its baseline; the six pseudo-flags (SECURITY runs the host exe itself) keep a flat 1800 s (300 s for WINDOWSOAK-JUDGE), so a spinning mutant on them runs 30 minutes
A timed-out MODULE-SELFTESTS or TEMPLATE run kills only powershell.exe; the host exe it launched keeps running (a spinning mutant included), holding module DLLs locked for the cases after it

Restore lives only in process memory: a hard kill mid-case strands the mutant in the source tree, and a later direct run neither detects nor repairs it (only the shard controller's git diff check does)
Test-ModuleSourceDiscovery and Test-ModulePublishFreshness share one try, so a discovery failure skips the freshness check and is reported under the freshness script's name
fix_direction: Split into two try/catch blocks, each adding its own script name to $failures, so the freshness check runs and is reported even when discovery fails.

title: The evidence directory is created before the run lock is taken, so a held or stale lock leaves an empty evidence directory and no results.json
Four of six variants carry no failure label, so any failing check in the focused fake suite counts the mutant as killed

The poke-sass check asserts only that 'RaiseSpeechRequest' precedes '.Say(' in the branch; the condition that makes the bubble a FALLBACK is never asserted, so inverting it (dropping the !) passes and silences every poke sass on a default install

The AgentFlow tick check asserts only that the copy statement exists and that the literal 'Inspect(ArgvPath' is absent; nothing asserts the worker's Inspect call takes argvPathNow, so a worker that reads the live property any other way passes

The NoteFullscreenScan check asserts the textual order thread-test < Post < last inline raise, but not the return that ends the worker branch, so deleting that return (a worker scan then posts AND raises inline on the worker) passes

The F159 'swept on a pool thread' clause matches Task.Run(delegate { then (?s).* to SweepOrphanedExtractions(); anywhere later in the sliced body, so it passes when the sweep call sits after the delegate has closed, on the UI thread
The GDI/USER/handle leak verdict reads only the app's self-reported settledSeries and never checks it is non-degenerate; the header still says the gate watches from OUTSIDE
fix_direction: Reject a settled series whose gdi/user/handles are below 1 (or far below the driver's concurrent external sample), and reword the header to say the in-process settled series decides GDI/USER/handles.

title: The whole shipped-payload half of the AgentBroker packaging test runs nowhere: nothing in the repo passes -CheckPayload
fix_direction: Have the gate call Test-AgentBrokerPackaging.ps1 -CheckPayload after the module build, or move the apphost-start and ZIP-size assertions into Publish-AgentBrokerWorker.ps1 and delete the unreachable block.

title: The CLOSES-WHEN arm reads only BACKLOG.md, which holds zero criteria at e20decd, while the one live criterion moved to docs/BLOCKED.md:294 in 6bb1002 and has not been evaluated since

Each run leaves a full editor-probe-<id> preparation (copied extension.js/package.json, manifest, workspace) plus an ordinary-junction-target directory under artifacts/agentbroker-editor-probes, never removed or reported

'foreign workspace refuses before read' points at a file that does not exist, so any refusal (scope check, parent check, or plain file-not-found in Read-ProbeText) satisfies it; it cannot tell a scope guard from a missing file
Test-CompletedWorkerBinaryCleanup.ps1 creates artifacts/worker-cleanup-tests-<guid> holding a git repository, a registered worktree, receipts and a sentinel, and never removes it on pass or failure
The 'restores environment on failure' half of Test-InstallerCompilerEnvironment triggers a refusal that fires before the builder touches the environment, so its restore assertion cannot fail
The finally block can replace the real failure with a cleanup exception and leave the outside target behind exactly when the guard it tests has failed
Each run leaves build/scoped-shutdown-tests/<guid> with six copies of the synthetic companion exe plus logs; nothing removes it
The 40-odd in-memory checks of the MSI API logging probe run only by hand: no gate, CI step or runner invokes this script
fix_direction: Run it from Invoke-OfflineScriptChecks.ps1 in a pwsh child judged by exit code (it is #requires 7 and uses Add-Type), as that runner already does for Test-PublicCommitPrivacy.ps1, together with A0330's Test-IsolatedMsiApiLoggingCase.ps1.

title: Test-IsolatedMsiApiLoggingCase.ps1 has no caller: no gate, CI step or other script runs it, so its 40-odd orchestration checks of Invoke-IsolatedMsiApiLoggingCase.ps1 guard nothing unless run by hand

A second -Apply on an already-applied fixture always fails at the foreign-image copy, but only after it has installed v1 and overwritten that fixture's logs, and its report then attributes the previous run's rollback-v2 registry failures to itself

The two 'mixed union requires a completed import / scheduled work' checks pass whether or not Assert-MixedShardCoverage's remainder_selection_empty guard exists, because Refuses accepts any exception and both fixtures also leave a coverage gap
The registry-namespace concurrency probe is invoked by no gate, CI step, harness or doc, and needs pwsh 7.4 while it declares #requires -Version 7

The capture checks for mutation_process.py (the byte-capture helper every mutation harness grades through) run only by hand: neither run-gate.ps1, Invoke-IsolatedGate.ps1 nor any workflow invokes run_mutation_capture_checks.py or this file

The mutation-infrastructure unit tests (test_mutation_capture_harnesses.py and the four sibling test_mutation_*.py modules, including test_mutation_caseplan for mutation_caseplan.py) are run by no gate, CI step or controller self-test; only a manual RELEASE-CHECKLIST line and tests/run_mutation_capture_checks.py, which nothing calls, invoke them
The legacy PowerShell witness skips its run_text half without saying so when the ANSI code page is not cp1252
The MCP transport probe's result fields NoExistingBrokerAccessed, ClientConfigurationRead, ProductChanged and ListenerAndClientDisposed are constants, not observations
Test-HostMsiUpgrade.ps1 and Stop-MutationPoolForHandoff.ps1 are one-shot tools hard-wired to gitignored artifacts of past runs (and a fixed controller PID), and nothing in the repository calls them

A prompt waiting in a VS Code panel is announced twice in Notify mode, once by the screen sweep and again by the transcript path about 20 s later, because the two one-shots (_announcedScreenPrompt and NotifyBudget's session/call keys) never consult each other

Every screen prompt carries the foreground window's TITLE and the title of the window the companion stands on verbatim, on every engine (local, cloud, CLI), while the background-window list deliberately sends process names only because 'a title is where the personal data lives'

Three places where the shipped test double cannot reproduce what the real host does, so a module self-test written against it passes for behaviour the app would refuse or lose (no in-tree module is hit today)
PrepareMembers parses every member's whole configuration twice, once only to read its RuntimeSchema and once to build it, and each parse already reads every document twice
The Ceiling-branch comment cites FormCompanion.cs:1327 (HORIZONTAL at the top) and :1258 (TASKBAR at the bottom); at e20decd those raises are at FormCompanion.cs:1508 and :1439
RootAttributesIgnored's header says a configuration root's text 'is still refused', but the next case (StrayTextIgnored) asserts root text converts to the same bytes and says it replaced that refusal

handoff.md's header says 'Last updated 2026-09-25' and its START HERE says v1.2.5 is the published release and catalog app.version is 1.2.5; the file was edited as late as 2026-11-04 (104a0e8) and the tree is host 1.11.0 with catalog app.version 1.11.0
Selection is uniform per LINE, not per pack: with the full catalog on, one pack (showerthoughts, 9,752 rows) supplies about one fortune in six, while a 2-row pack appears about once in 28,000 draws
The fortune loader's whole-library caps are about half used by today's catalog: 158 packs, 8.31 MB and 55,783 entries against 16 MiB and 100,000
The SCOPE note says --module-selftest runs for 'all seven in-tree modules' and the tray is shared by 'six modules'; the covered set is eight

Every catalog fetch, including the unprompted launch checks, answers a proxy 407 with the signed-in user's Windows credentials, so a WPAD-discovered proxy on an untrusted network can collect an NTLM exchange
The Pingus gallery blurb says it has 'the most moves outside the sheep club (28!)', while the same map's converted-Shimeji blurbs describe catalog pets with forty and sixty-six animations

Where a recording's transcript goes is fixed at the moment Stop is pressed: changing 'Summary runs on', switching the summary off or turning the follow-up off while that recording transcribes (up to 6 hours) does not stop it reaching the CLI or cloud vendor

The downloaded whisper-cli zip is verified only when GitHub's API happens to report a digest, silently skipped otherwise, and the 75-466 MB model has no integrity check beyond a size floor; both are then executed/loaded by TryVerify

'Put windows back' identifies a window by its bare HWND value only: a recorded window that was closed and whose handle value was later reused would be moved (and restored from minimised) as if it were the original

Pack scoping isolates members of packs, but every packless tick type shares one namespace keyed by its pet id: a packless companion's TransformMascot or BornMascot that names another loaded packless companion's id turns into, or breeds, that other author's companion

LifecycleAdapter.SubmitAsync's comment says its delivery failure still faults the runtime's delivery loop and shutdown reports it, which the same file's comment at :49-51 and its RUNTIME_DELIVERY_FAULT_SETTLES check (:72) say is no longer true

Two docstring claims in mutate-agentflow.py are false for this file: the line_ending_variant history was pasted from mutate-hardening-guards.py, and 'every child runs with a private TEMP' does not hold for the build children
run_gate is the one child in either harness with no timeout: a stalled powershell.exe hangs the run with the mutant still in src/ instead of reading BROKEN

The preflight evidence's ScopedShutdownSafe is the literal $true on the only path that writes it, so the caller's `ScopedShutdownSafe -ne $true` refusal (Invoke-IsolatedMsiApiLoggingCase.ps1:123) can never fire; the safety verdict rests entirely on the script throwing

lifecycle-result.json's InstalledApplicationTouched is the constant $false, written in every report, and the fixture's isolation leaves the production ProgramsFolder (the real LocalAppData Programs folder) un-redirected
Direction collapse can merge an embedded jump into a stationary pose
fix_direction: Add QualifiesAsJump(Source) to the CollapseDirectionPairs match key alongside IsGaze, so a jump never merges with a non-jump. Build jumpConverted from the emitted spokes, not from config.Actions. Add a self-test fixture with a byte-identical jump-and-rest pair, mutation-checked.

title: Ceiling frames can be silently cropped by floor-based cell height
fix_direction: In Compose, measure each AnchorToTop frame's overflow (sh - srcY - scaledCellH) and name the clipped frames and rows in the residue, or refuse or scale those frames. Add a self-test fixture with a ceiling sprite that extends below its anchor further than the floor anchor height, and correct the unenforced claim at PetEmitter.cs:1239-1244.

title: Matching traces may omit a scenario starter and still compare exact
fix_direction: When compare() is given a scenario, require each trace's tick-0 sids, in order, to equal [m["sid"] for m in scenario["mascots"]] (unjudgeable or entity-mismatch), and add a self-test row that drops the second starter from both traces.

title: V1 does not validate private draft dependencies against the pinned archive
fix_direction: In validate_v1_build/v1_prepare (and bridge), take lib/*.jar and conf/ entries from source-inventory.json, verify each private-source file's hash against it, refuse extra or missing files, and add a v1_self_test witness for a drifted library.

title: Surface repeat cap can fall short of the promised crossing distance
fix_direction: Raise MaxSurfaceRepeats to at least ceil(SurfaceReachPx/SurfacePxPerStep) (667, within the runtime's MaximumRepeat 1000) or derive the cap from stepsNeeded. Then add a one-frame travelling ceiling fixture, plus a reach assertion on the flat-wall synthesised climber, both checking SurfaceReachOf >= SurfaceReachTargetPx.

title: Older Shared runner does not contain scenario-derived output paths
fix_direction: Derive the Shared run folder with v1_run_directory-style checks (V1_SCENARIO_ID fullmatch plus v1_contained) and require doc["id"] to equal the hardcoded file stem before any mkdir, then add a self-test case that expects the refusal.
